idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Why Your Toilet Keeps Running: The Flapper Seal Failure
description: A continuously running toilet is most commonly caused by a faulty flapper seal at the base of the tank. Over time, chloramines in municipal water, drop-in tank cleaners, or mineral deposits degrade the rubber flapper. When it warps or hardens, it fails to form a watertight seal against the flush valve seat, allowing water to trickle continuously into the bowl. As the tank water level drops, the float lowers, triggering the fill valve to run repeatedly. Before replacing the entire fill valve mechanism, check the flapper for warping, mineral crust, or improper chain tension. Have you inspected your tank flapper lately?

The primary focus is near the bottom center of the tank, showing the flush valve assembly and a flexible rubber flapper seal. The flapper is slightly lifted on one edge, illustrating a tiny gap between the rubber seal and the plastic flush valve seat where water escapes into the flush opening below. The fill valve, overflow tube, and float cup are visible inside the tank in realistic detail. Clean bright lighting, studio background, soft shadows, realistic plumbing materials including ceramic, molded plastic, and rubber. Completely free of text, numbers, arrows, visual labels, brand names, logos, or watermarks. Ample empty visual space at top and bottom for text placement.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear cutaway view of a toilet tank to highlight the flapper valve at the bottom of the tank. Viewers can see how a warped or improperly seated flapper creates a small gap at the flush valve seat, demonstrating visually why water leaks continuously from the tank into the bowl and forces the fill valve to stay open.

on_image_text.explanation: A hardened or warped rubber flapper prevents a watertight seal at the flush valve seat.
on_image_text.takeaway: Inspect and clean or replace the flapper before buying a new fill valve assembly.
